title: Validation and Comparative Multi-Omics Benchmarking of Fluid-Derived Volatilomics Biomarkers for the Prevention and Early Detection of Schizophrenia
summary: Schizophrenia is one of the most severe mental disorders. It is characterized by psychotic symptoms, such as paranoia and hallucinations, especially hearing voices. Diagnosing SZ is not trivial. Not everyone who experiences psychosis will receive a schizophrenia diagnosis. According to current diagnostic criteria, at least six months of observation after the onset of psychosis is needed for a schizophrenia diagnosis. SZ also lacks objective signs (biomarkers) of the disease, so the diagnosis is made clinically. Recently, a new field of diagnostics based on volatile organic compounds has emerged. This method involves analyzing biological fluids, such as blood, urine, and sweat, or expiratory air, using portable devices. Several studies have shown the potential of this diagnostic method in detecting several psychiatric diseases, including schizophrenia. In this study, we plan to observe patients with first-episode psychosis. This patient group, along with healthy participants and patients with depression, will be monitored using clinical interviews, scales, volatilomics, genomics, proteomics, and other laboratory-based diagnostics within two years. Ultimately, we hope to identify schizophrenia biomarkers that could enable early diagnosis of the disease.

interventions.name: This is a multi-center, naturalistic, register study. No interventions. Following groups of participants are planned: Patients with acute Psychosis not fullfilling the SZ criteria - 610, Patient with SZ diagnoses - 610, Clinical High-Risk Group 120, Patients with depression or bipolar disorder - 564

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age: 16–55 years.
Diagnosis based on DSM-5 criteria
Informed Written Consent.
Healthy Controls and Relatives of Patients with SZ and BP.
Exclusion criteria:
Actual Suicidality
Cognitive Impairment
Eating Disorder
Severe Internal Disorders for Healthy Controls
Any Current Mental Health Condition or History of Major Mental Health Disorder for Healthy Controls and Relatives.
